title: Balanced Binary Tree
statement: You get the root of a binary tree. Say whether it is height-balanced: at every node, the heights of the left and right subtrees differ by at most 1. An empty tree counts as balanced.

example.caption: Node 20 has two leaves, and node 3 has heights 1 and 2. Every node differs by at most 1, so the tree is balanced.

idea.sentence: Compute each node's height, and while you are there, check that its two sides differ by at most 1.

jargon.plain: No node has one side more than 1 level taller than the other. It is a rule about every node, not just the root.
How many nodes are on the longest path from a node down to a leaf. A lone leaf is 1.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the tree as a level-order array, null for a missing child, e.g. [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]

compare.bruteLabel: Measure both subtrees from scratch at every node
compare.optimalLabel: One pass: height and check together
compare.unit: node visits, for a skinny tree

rows.name: Measure at every node
rows.note: Each node calls a separate height function that walks its whole subtree.

rows.name: Height and check in one pass
rows.note: Each node is visited once. The child heights come back from the recursion.

fast.takeaway: Asking for a height and then asking again at the parent repeats work. Return the height once and check on the way up.

stages.title: Start balanced
stages.note: balanced is true until some node proves otherwise. It lives outside the recursion.

stages.title: Heights below
stages.note: Recurse left and right. Each call returns the height of its subtree.

stages.title: Compare the sides
stages.note: If the two heights differ by more than 1, this node is lopsided. Set balanced to false.

stages.title: Report up
stages.note: Return 1 + the taller side as this node's height. At the end, balanced is the answer.

edges.title: Empty tree
edges.why: There is no node to be lopsided.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: Both sides have height 0. The difference is 0.

edges.title: Equal at the top, bad below
edges.why: The root sees heights 4 and 4, which look fine. Node 2 on the left has heights 3 and 0. You must check every node.

edges.title: Leaning chain
edges.why: Node 1 has a left height of 2 and a right height of 0. A difference of 2 is too much.

gotchas.text: Checking only the root is wrong. A tree can have equal heights at the root and still hide a lopsided node deeper down.
The limit is 1, so a difference of exactly 1 is fine. Use > 1, not >= 1.
Calling a separate height function at every node works but costs O(n^2) on a skinny tree. Return the height from the same recursion instead.
Math.abs(left - right) is clear. If you write left - right > 1 alone you miss the case where right is taller.
Go has no integer abs in the standard library. Compare with left-right > 1 || right-left > 1.

recap.key: Return the height, and clear a balanced flag whenever the two side heights differ by more than 1.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(h) call stack.
moves: left, right = heights of the two children
If they differ by more than 1, balanced = false. Return 1 + max(left, right)
